title: FREAK Academy Reference
description: V3-first reference skeleton for the browser Academy connector. This artifact is intentionally compact until the full Book and Reference routes exist.

entries.title: Program Output
entries.summary: `say` writes a value followed by a newline in the V3 Academy subset.
staticSemantics: The expression must parse and type-check before the program can run.
The V3 Academy worker currently checks output through exact expected-output requirements.
dynamicSemantics: At runtime, `say` evaluates its expression and writes the rendered value to standard output.
The learner compares the complete stdout text against the lesson's expected output.

entries.title: Word Literals
entries.summary: A `word` literal is UTF-8 text enclosed in double quotes.
staticSemantics: A double-quoted literal has type `word` in the current Academy subset.
dynamicSemantics: The runtime preserves the literal text and prints it without the surrounding quotes.

entries.title: Variable Declarations
entries.summary: `pilot` declares a local value that can be reused by later expressions.
staticSemantics: The initializer expression determines the value assigned to the local name.
An optional annotation constrains the inferred type.
dynamicSemantics: The initializer runs once when the declaration is reached.

entries.title: Primitive Types
entries.summary: The first Academy lessons use `int` and `word` as the practical V3 starter types.
staticSemantics: `int` represents signed integer values in the V3 Academy subset.
A type annotation makes the intended type explicit.
dynamicSemantics: Primitive values can be printed directly with `say` in the starter lessons.

examples.title: Use explicit types
examples.source:
pilot label: word = "power"
pilot amount: int = 42
say label
say amount

entries.title: Expressions and Operators
entries.summary: Binary operators combine expressions into a new value.
staticSemantics: The operands must be valid expressions for the operator being used.
dynamicSemantics: Arithmetic expressions evaluate before their result is printed or assigned.

entries.title: Conditionals
entries.summary: `if` chooses a branch from a boolean condition.
staticSemantics: The condition must be a valid boolean expression.
The current Academy lessons use comparison expressions for the condition.

examples.title: Choose a branch

entries.title: Repeat Loops
entries.summary: `repeat N times` runs a block a fixed number of times.
staticSemantics: The count must be valid for the V3 counted-loop subset.
dynamicSemantics: The loop body runs once per count, in order.

entries.title: Task Declarations
entries.summary: `task` declares reusable behavior with optional parameters and a return value.
staticSemantics: Parameter and return annotations describe the task boundary.
`give back` must provide a value compatible with the task return type.
dynamicSemantics: Calling a task evaluates its body and returns the value from `give back`.
